extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/patent practitioners (prosecution attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO/MPEP guidance on transitional after-final submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a) and Request for Continued Examination (RCE) practice under 37 CFR 1.114: eligibility, what counts as a submission, timing and fee requirements, examiner processing, and limits on use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for transitional practice under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is subject to the provisions of Public Law 103-465, effective June 8, 1995. The application must have been filed on or before June 8, 1995 and have been pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (taking into account any reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c)); for applications entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 or filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 of a PCT application designating the U.S., the PCT international filing date will be used to determine pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.41.01.fti may be used to notify applicant that the application qualifies under 37 CFR 1.129(a). Do not use the form paragraph in design or reissue applications, or in reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to have first submission entered under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is entitled to have a first submission after final rejection entered and considered on the merits if the submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an Appeal Brief under 37 CFR 41.37 and prior to abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon timely filing of the submission and appropriate fee the finality of the previous Office action will be withdrawn. If a notice of appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with the payment, payment of 1.17(r) will be construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and continue prosecution under 1.129(a). In view of 35 U.S.C. 132, no amendment considered as a result of the payment may introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible content of a 37 CFR 1.129(a) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) may comprise, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims or drawings, a new substantive argument and/or new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee under 1.17(r) may introduce new matter into the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132). If applicant files multiple proposed amendments that conflict, applicant should provide specific instructions for entry or non-entry upon payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of previously refused IDS when using 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDS previously refused consideration because of applicant’s failure to comply with 37 CFR 1.97(c) or (d) will be treated as though it has been filed within one of the time periods set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(b) and will be considered without the petition and petition fee required in 1.97(d), if it complies with 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any IDS submitted under 1.129(a) on or after June 8, 2005 without a statement specified in 1.97(e) will be treated as though it had been filed within the time period set forth in 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 1.17(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may introduce new rejection based on IDS (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may introduce a new ground of rejection based on the information submitted in the IDS and make the next Office action final provided that the examiner introduces no other new ground of rejection which has not been necessitated by amendment to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a) for application of second-action-final practice where IDS is basis for new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of conditional payment of the 1.17(r) fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' payment of the fee (authorization to charge deposit account or credit card in the event the submission would not otherwise be entered), the Office will treat the conditional payment as an unconditional payment of the 1.17(r) fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon the timely filing of the submission and payment of the 1.17(r) fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering and entry of previously unentered submissions after 1.17(r) payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon timely payment of the 1.17(r) fee, all previously unentered submissions, and submissions filed with the 1.17(r) fee will be entered in the order in which they were filed absent specific instructions for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any conflicting amendments should be clarified for entry by the applicant upon payment of the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsiveness to prior Office action under 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines that the submission is not fully responsive to the previous Office action (e.g., submission only includes an IDS), applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of the letter to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shortened statutory period supersedes the time period set in the prior Office action and may be extended pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a). If a notice of appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with payment of 1.17(r), payment is construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and to continue prosecution; the appeal stands dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of first action following submission filed prior to June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission and payment of the 1.17(r) fee, the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.03.fti may be used if it is appropriate to make the first action final following a submission under 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of action following submission filed on or after June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: For timely submission and payment of the 1.17(r) fee on or after June 8, 2005, the next Office action on the merits will be equivalent to the next Office action following a reply to a non-final Office action; such an Office action will be made final except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the period set forth in 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a). Form paragraph 7.42.031.fti may be used to make the next Office action final following a submission under 1.129(a) filed on or after June 8, 2005.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period rules for replies to final actions after 1.129(a) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period for reply to a final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date of the action. If a first reply is filed within TWO MONTHS and the advisory action is mailed after the three-month period, the shortened period will expire on the date the advisory action is mailed; in no event will the reply period expire later than SIX MONTHS from the mailing date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is reminded of extension of time policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a); extension fees are calculated from mailing date of advisory action when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of 1.129(a) submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant whose application is eligible for the transitional procedure under 37 CFR 1.129(a) is entitled to consideration of two after-final submissions. If one submission has been filed and the application is again under a final rejection, the applicant is entitled to one additional submission; if two submissions have been filed and the application is again under a final rejection, no additional submissions under 1.129(a) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be entitled to consideration of an additional submission only if the submission meets the conditions set forth in 37 CFR 1.116. If the 1.17(r) fee has been twice paid, the provisions of 1.129(a) are no longer available and subsequent submissions will be treated per current after-final practice in 37 CFR 1.116.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis and fee policy for RCE (35 U.S.C. 132(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(b) provides for the continued examination of applications at the request of the applicant upon payment of a fee; the Director may establish fees and shall provide a 50 percent reduction in such fees for qualifying small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented in part via 37 CFR 1.114 and 1.17(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and exclusions for RCE under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.114 apply to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE provisions do not apply to a provisional application; an application for a utility or plant patent filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before June 8, 1995; an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before June 8, 1995, or an international application that does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 371; an application for a design patent; an international design application; or a patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.114(e) for excluded categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for filing an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may obtain continued examination by filing a request for continued examination, a submission, and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: (1) payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 1.313 is granted); (2) abandonment of the application; or (3) filing of a notice of appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146, unless the appeal or civil action is terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed after appeal but prior to a decision on the appeal, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner. An appeal brief or reply brief will not be considered a submission under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution must be closed before filing an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution in an application is closed as used in this section if the application is under appeal, or the last Office action is a final action (37 CFR 1.113), a notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.311), or an action that otherwise closes prosecution in the application (e.g., Ex parte Quayle action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant cannot request continued examination until after prosecution is closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as a 'submission' for RCE purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability. If a reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for suspension of action, an appeal brief or a reply brief (or related papers) will not be considered a submission under 1.114, though arguments in a previously filed appeal or reply brief may be incorporated by reference to satisfy submission requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously entered arguments to satisfy RCE submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments submitted after final rejection that were entered by the examiner but not found persuasive may satisfy the submission requirement if such arguments are responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of whether any submission is responsive to the last outstanding Office action is done without factoring in the 'final' status of such outstanding Office action; thus replies unacceptable under 1.113 may be acceptable under 1.111 for RCE purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE cannot be used to switch to an independent and distinct invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions). Any newly submitted claims directed to an invention independent and distinct from the invention previously claimed will be withdrawn from consideration and not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.145 for conversion/withdrawal of such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE is not a new application and will not be converted to one
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is not the filing of a new application. The Office will not convert an RCE to a new application such as an application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat RCE as request to continue examination of same application, not to restart prosecution as new file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath/declaration requirement for national stage RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: For an effective request for continued examination in a 35 U.S.C. 371 national stage application, all required inventor’s oaths or declarations (or substitute statements) must be submitted in the application prior to or with the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with 37 CFR 1.114(e), an RCE cannot be filed in an international application that does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 371; 371(c)(4) requires submission of the oath or declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checks for RCE filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel will verify that: (A) the application is a utility or plant application (not design); (B) the application was filed on or after June 8, 1995; (C) prosecution is closed; (D) the RCE was filed before payment of the issue fee or, if not, a petition under 1.313 was filed and granted; (E) the application was pending when the RCE was filed; (F) the RCE was accompanied by the proper fee(s) including RCE fee under 1.17(e); (G) the RCE included a submission as required by 1.114; and (H) if national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, a compliant inventor's oath/declaration for each inventor was submitted prior to or with the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE will not be processed if the application is undergoing court review at the Federal Circuit or in federal district court because the application is in the jurisdiction of the court and the RCE procedure is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCE filings
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE have not been satisfied, applicant will be so notified. Generally, a 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE),' Form PTO-2051, will be mailed to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural notice rather than acceptance of RCE; follow-up actions depend on reason(s) for impropriety.
